title: Insufficient Quality of Mental Health Information on German-Speaking TikTok: A Content Analysis
screen_reason: Content analysis of 177 German-language TikTok videos drawn from the six most-viewed mental-disorder hashtags, each rated by two clinical psychologists against diagnostic criteria as correct / overgeneralized / incorrect / subjective experience, with verbatim shares (33.3%, n=59 incorrect; 18.1%, n=32 overgeneralized) over an explicit 177-video denominator. Meets the CONTENT criterion; the mDISCERN and GQS means are additionally recorded as QUALITY rows.

estimates.country: German-language (German-speaking) TikTok; authorship categories defined by reference to German social law
estimates.date: Hashtag view ranking taken 4 January 2024; videos downloaded 4 January to 14 February 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of top German-language TikTok videos under six mental-disorder hashtags rated as presenting incorrect information
estimates.denominator: 177 German-language TikTok videos: the first 30 videos returned by the TikTok algorithm for each of the six most-viewed German mental-disorder hashtags (#ADHS, #Depression, #Autismus, #Angststoerung, #Narzissmus, #PTBS), i.e. 180 downloaded minus 3 unratable
estimates.definition: Rated 'Incorrect' = 'Presents symptoms that are not symptoms of the disorder or common phenomena of daily life or wrong information'. Videos containing both incorrect information and subjective descriptions were rated as incorrect.
estimates.misinfo_def: The paper does not give a general definition of misinformation; it operationalises it as a video that 'presents symptoms that are not symptoms of the disorder or common phenomena of daily life or wrong information', in contrast to 'correct' videos that 'present core symptoms of and information on the disorder correctly'.
estimates.source_quote: Of the 177 Videos, 19.2% (n = 34) were rated as correct, 33.3% (n = 59) as incorrect, 18.1% (n = 32) as overgeneralized and 29.4% (n = 52) as personal experience.
estimates.page_loc: Results, 'Basic Video Characteristics' (p. 7); also Abstract, Results
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Independent ratings by two clinical psychologists with in- and outpatient diagnostic experience (AM, BL), using a four-level scheme carried over from Yeung et al. (2022) and Aragon-Guevara et al. (2025) and judged against diagnostic criteria (DSM-5); disagreements resolved by mutual consent (19 videos, 17 of which differed by one level). Cohen's kappa on the initial independent quality ratings = .813 (p < .001).
estimates.moderator_quote: To achieve a comprehensive overview of viral mental health topics on TikTok, a TikTok account was created to follow the six German-language hashtags about mental disorders that have the highest overall views (see Figure 1). ... For each disorder, the first 30 German videos were included, sorted by the proprietary TikTok app algorithm. ... From January 4th, 2024, to February 14th, 2024, a total of 180 videos were downloaded for assessment ... Three videos were excluded, resulting in 177 included videos.
estimates.notes: 59/177 = 33.3%, matching the verbatim value. denom_selection=curated because the sample is a rank-truncated top-30-per-hashtag set chosen by the TikTok algorithm ('chosen to be representative of the experience a user might have searching for a diagnosis on TikTok'), not a random or census sample of German mental-health TikTok. Country coded Germany although strictly the frame is German-LANGUAGE TikTok (which also reaches Austria and Switzerland); the authors anchor their authorship categories in German law. The categories correct / overgeneralized / incorrect / subjective experience are mutually exclusive, so 33.3% is the strict-falsity share only.

estimates.date: Hashtag view ranking taken 4 January 2024; videos downloaded 4 January to 14 February 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of the same 177 videos rated as overgeneralized (misleading but not outright wrong)
estimates.definition: Rated 'Overgeneralized' = 'Presents symptoms and information that are typical for mental disorders but do not belong to core symptoms of the disorder or describes undifferentiated and overgeneralized symptoms'.
estimates.misinfo_def: See primary row; 'overgeneralized' is the authors' intermediate category between correct and incorrect, which they describe collectively with 'incorrect' as 'incorrect or misleading information'.
estimates.source_quote: Of the 177 Videos, 19.2% (n = 34) were rated as correct, 33.3% (n = 59) as incorrect, 18.1% (n = 32) as overgeneralized and 29.4% (n = 52) as personal experience.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two clinical-psychologist raters and the same consensus procedure; kappa .813 on the initial quality ratings.
estimates.moderator_quote: Overgeneralized: Presents symptoms and information that are typical for mental disorders but do not belong to core symptoms of the disorder or describes undifferentiated and overgeneralized symptoms.
estimates.notes: DISJOINT, NOT NESTED: 'overgeneralized' and 'incorrect' are mutually exclusive categories of the same 177 videos, so this row must NOT be read as a broader definition containing the 33.3% row - it is the looser-falsity category on its own. The authors' own combined statement is qualitative ('Over 50% of the screened videos include incorrect or misleading information'; 'more than half of the videos were incorrect or overgeneralized'); I did not create a combined 51.4% row because 59+32 would be a cross-category sum, which R8 forbids. An adjudicator wanting a single broad-definition value should use the authors' 'over 50%' wording rather than a computed figure.

estimates.measure_type: Mean Global Quality Scale (GQS) score of the 177 videos (5-point scale, higher = better)
estimates.definition: Global Quality Scale: a five-point Likert scale from 'very poor quality' to 'excellent quality', based on video quality, flow of information and usefulness of information for patients.
estimates.misinfo_def: n/a - this is a quality instrument, not a falsity judgement.
estimates.source_quote: The videos showed an average GQS of 1.82 (SD = .966, range 1 - 5) and mDISCERN of 1.34 (SD = .655, range 1 - 4).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Rated by the same two clinical psychologists; no separate reliability statistic is reported for the GQS (the kappa of .813 refers to the correctness ratings).
estimates.moderator_quote: For a quantitative assessment of the quality of the information for patients, videos were rated by the same two raters on the Global Quality Scale (GQS ...), a five-point Likert scale ranging from 'very poor quality' to 'excellent quality' based on video quality, flow of information ... and usefulness of information.
estimates.notes: QUALITY row - a mean scale score, not a share; excluded from prevalence pooling. Recorded because the schema provides for GQS/DISCERN-type instruments.

estimates.measure_type: Mean modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) reliability score of the 177 videos (5-point scale, higher = more reliable)
estimates.definition: Modified DISCERN: five yes/no questions (understandability, validity of cited sources, unbiased/balanced content, additional sources, mention of uncertainty) giving a maximum of five points, from 'unreliable' to 'very reliable'.
estimates.misinfo_def: n/a - reliability instrument, not a falsity judgement.
estimates.source_quote: The videos showed an average GQS of 1.82 (SD = .966, range 1 - 5) and mDISCERN of 1.34 (SD = .655, range 1 - 4).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Rated by the same two clinical psychologists; no separate reliability statistic reported for the mDISCERN.
estimates.moderator_quote: Reliability of the information provided in the videos was assessed using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) ... supplying a five-point Likert scale ranging from 'unreliable' to 'very reliable'.
estimates.notes: QUALITY row - a mean scale score, not a share; excluded from prevalence pooling.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (1) the two remaining rating categories of the same 177 videos - correct 19.2% (n=34) and subjective/personal experience 29.4% (n=52) - which are not misinformation shares (the 'subjective experience' category is a large, unclassified-for-truth residual that mechanically depresses both the correct and the incorrect share, and an adjudicator should note it); (2) a combined 'incorrect or overgeneralized' figure (91/177 = 51.4%), which the authors assert only qualitatively ('Over 50% of the screened videos include incorrect or misleading information'; 'With around half of the analyzed videos supplying incorrect information') - a cross-category sum, forbidden by R8; (3) authorship shares (experts 32/177, 18.1%; affected persons 88/177, 49.7%; laypeople 57/177, 32.2%) - producer composition, not falsity; (4) the per-disorder and per-authorship GQS/mDISCERN means in Table 2, and the statement that 'every single video on narcissism contained misinformation' with narcissism 'showing exclusively incorrect or overgeneralized information' - Figures 2 and 3 hold the per-disorder and per-authorship rating COUNTS but are images, so the underlying cell counts (e.g. how many of the 30 narcissism videos were incorrect vs overgeneralized) are not in the text layer and cannot be extracted verbatim; (5) view and like counts (94,348,220 views total, mean 533,040 per video) - reach of the videos, but no misinformation-specific denominator, so no EXPOSURE row is derivable; (6) the 90%-of-ADHD-test-videos figure attributed to Verma & Sinha (2025) and the 'at least half' figures attributed to other studies in the Introduction - values cited from elsewhere, excluded by R8.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Sampling frame: a purpose-made TikTok account followed the six German-language mental-disorder hashtags with the highest cumulative views as of 4 January 2024; the first 30 German videos per hashtag in the app's algorithmic order were taken, 180 downloaded 4 Jan-14 Feb 2024 via ssstik.io, 3 excluded as not ratable against diagnostic criteria, leaving 177. No a priori sample size; a G*Power sensitivity analysis indicated 80% power for small-to-medium effects (w = .277). Coding procedure: two clinical psychologists rated each video independently as correct / overgeneralized / incorrect / subjective experience, plus authorship (expert / affected person / layperson), plus GQS and mDISCERN; disagreements (19 videos) settled by mutual consent. Reliability as reported: Cohen's kappa .813 (p < .001) on the initial quality ratings; no reliability reported for GQS, mDISCERN or authorship. No ethics approval (public material); not preregistered; data available on request. Author-declared limitations: only 30 videos per disorder; narcissistic personality disorder is not an ICD diagnosis; German-language only.
